verdicts.evidence: The logbook implements the spiked-cumulant model at d=800, alpha={15,30}, and shows PCA/linear autoencoder theta_v values at the d^{-1/2} floor (0.042, 0.031 at k*=2; 0.015, 0.006 at k*=3), confirming the hidden spike v* is invisible to PCA while the visible spike u* resides in the covariance.

Real experiments at d=800 (paper uses d=2000) with only k*=2 and k*=3 tested: ReLU recovers v* convincingly at k*=2 (0.134→0.184 vs floor 0.035) but at k*=3 tanh is only marginally above floor (0.058, ~1.65×), and recovery of u* by the nonlinear AE is not reported; the 'provably' theoretical aspect is not addressed by numerical experiments.
No AMP experiments appear anywhere in the logbook; the executive summary explicitly lists AMP as part of the 'Full replication' scope not undertaken in this reproduction.

No spherical gradient flow experiments are present; the logbook uses full-batch Adam instead, and no convergence-time scaling with d is measured. Gradient-flow theory is listed as out-of-scope for this reproduction.

At k*=2, d=800, alpha=30: linear AE has lower test recon MSE (799.12 vs 800.11) yet higher downstream error (0.497 vs 0.451) and fails to recover v* (theta_v=0.031 vs 0.205), concretely demonstrating the misalignment between self-supervised test loss and representation quality.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical experiments supporting the core empirical phenomena—PCA invisibility of the hidden spike and test-loss/generalization misalignment—at a reduced but reasonable scale (d=800). It does not address the AMP or gradient-flow theoretical claims at all, and the k*=3 recovery results are marginal, matching the paper's own near-floor regime.
